summary: Kickoff for TransitFlow activation focused on observability, network intake, and a performance pilot. TransitFlow prefers private deployment options because of PII/regulatory concerns; they require SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and KMS integration. Redwood team (AE+SE+CSM) proposed a 3-week Dedicated pilot, benchmark plan, and next steps for network/security intake.
questions: Can Redwood run in TransitFlow VPC with no egress?
What's the expected p95 lat for 1024-token customer chat?
How are audit logs retained and exported?
Is HSM integration supported for customer-managed keys?
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-20 16:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jamie Lin (Redwood SE), Rae Carter (Redwood CSM), Alex Rivera (CTO), Priya Nair (Head of MLOps), Marcus Chen (Infra Lead), Olga Sokolov (Dir, Data Privacy)

Auto-summary: quick kickoff, network and security handoff, agree pilot and benchmarks.

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? we'll keep this to an hour, cover network, security, and a perf pilot.
00:12 Alex: Yep, Alex here, CTO at TransitFlow. We run on-prem k8s with a mix of GPU nodes, and we have strict data residency — most customer traces can't leave the VPC.
00:20 Priya: Priya here, running MLOps. Our main ask is sub-200ms median for short chat flows and predictable token cost; also we want observable token-level cost breakdown.
00:32 Samir: Great, that maps to our Dedicated offering or Private deployment. Jamie will talk tech details.
00:38 Jamie: Hi team. Quick note: we can do Private (VPC) or Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs in your cloud account) — apologies, I sometimes say "Dedicate" — streaming and caching will help lat. For the latency target you mentioned, we need to size batch windows and KV cash, sorry, KV cache to keep prefix hits.
00:58 Marcus: A couple network things — we don't want outbound internet from the GPU subnet. Can you do VPC peering with no egress?
01:04 Jamie: You can run Redwood Private with no public egress; we support private endpoints. If there are proxies, we can work with them — we just need the CIDR ranges and the proxy auth type.
01:20 Olga: Also, on encryption: we use customer-managed keys in AWS KMS and some workloads require HSM-backed keys. Is that supported?
01:28 Rae: We support KMS and HSM integrations for Private installs; for Hosted, we have our own KMS but can discuss BYOK for Dedicated in certain contracts. I'll send the security pack after this call.
01:40 Alex: Good. On observability, we want traces per-route and per-model latency breakdowns, plus token cost attribution so product can see unit economics.
01:50 Jamie: Console exposes per-route metrics; we can stream traces to your splunk or datadog, and we also emit token-level billing records. Caveat — the streaming exporter needs network whitelisting.
02:06 Marcus: About the perf pilot: what are assumptions? batch sizes, token lengths, seq length distribution — we have a lot of short queries but some long ones.
02:14 Jamie: For baseline we'll run a sweep: single-GPU with 512 and 1024 token sequences, varying concurrency to simulate latency and cost. We'll share the harness. Note: quantization helps cost but impacts accuracy; we'll show tradeoffs.
02:32 Priya: Can we do a canary model rollout? i.e., route 10% to a lower-cost quantized variant?
02:40 Samir: Yes — rollouts and automatic fallback policies are supported, you can pin version or do canary/A-B in the console. Important to have evaluation prompts to watch quality regressions.
02:52 Alex: On compliance — SOC2 and audit logs. We need exportable audit logs for requests and role changes. Also SSO: we use SAML (some folks call it sam el sometimes in notes).
03:02 Rae: We'll include SOC2 reports and the audit log schema. SAML SSO is supported; we also support SCIM for provisioning.
03:12 Olga: Retention policies — some data must be deleted on request in 48 hours, others we keep for 1 year for debugging. How flexible is retention?
03:22 Jamie: You can configure retention at the route level; for Private installs you control retention settings and we can help implement deletion workflows. We will document recommended retention settings in the runbook.
03:34 Marcus: One blocker: our infra team expects to run load tests from inside the VPC. Is there a way to attach a test harness to the private endpoint without going out to the internet?
03:42 Jamie: Yes, we can host the harness in your subnet or give you a dockerized harness that talks directly to the private endpoint. We'll need the cert thumbprint and endpoint FQDN.
03:54 Alex: Are there limits on concurrent requests per-pod? we have bursts from batch uploads.
04:02 Jamie: Autoscaling in Dedicated supports burst capacity and can scale pods; we recommend burst queues and rate limits configured in the console. We'll share autoscaling policy examples.
04:16 Priya: Cost question — is Dedicated always more expensive than Hosted? what's the math for token economics?
04:24 Samir: It depends on utilization. Hosted is easy but variable cost; Dedicated has a commit model. We'll share a cost model spreadsheet comparing per-token cost at different utilization rates. For heavy steady traffic Dedicated is typically better.
04:40 Alex: Any competitor gotchas we should watch for? we've looked at Anthropic and Bedrock.
04:46 Samir: Anthropic is strong on safety, Bedrock has convenience but variable perf across regions; we focus on predictable economics and observability for production. We'll include benchmark comparators in the doc.
04:58 Marcus: Network intake timeline: we can compile CIDR and proxy details by Monday (2026-08-22).
05:04 Samir: Great. To recap, we'll run a 3-week pilot: week 1 network & security hookup + baseline tests; week 2 perf tuning and quantization tests; week 3 canary rollout and SLA check.
05:18 Alex: Sounds good. One ask — can you also include an example Data Processing Addendum for our legal/compliance team?
05:24 Rae: Yes, we'll include a DPA and sample contract terms.
05:30 Olga: And include details of audit log fields so our auditors can map them.
05:36 Jamie: We'll export a sample CSV of audit events and the JSON schema.
05:42 Samir: I'll send the pilot agreement and pricing matrix after this. Any other questions?
05:48 Priya: One nit — do you have any guidance on model selection for reranking vs generation? we plan to use embeddings + rerank for search and a smaller generative model for chat.
05:58 Jamie: We recommend embeddings for semantic search, reranking for precision, and a more powerful decoder for chat. We'll attach a short decision tree doc.
06:10 Alex: OK thanks folks. Let's align on dates in calendar and expect the security pack tomorrow.
06:18 Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with action items.

End of transcript.
